title: When reoxygenation fails: a dynamical model of HIF-1 alpha -mediated metabolic breakdown under hypoxia and SARS-CoV-2 infection.
one_liner_zh: 该文构建HIF-1α介导的细胞代谢动力学模型，研究缺氧与SARS-CoV-2感染下的能量代谢转变，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Cells normally combine glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) to meet energy demands, but this balance shifts under pathological conditions. During SARS-CoV-2 infection, hypoxia, viral entry, and elevated tissue lactate alter cellular metabolism. To explore these effects, we propose a parsimonious mathematical model describing how oxygen levels, viral infiltration, and extracellular lactate jointly regulate metabolic balance through HIF-1 alpha protein, inside the cell, accounting for lactate's biphasic, non-monotonic influence on glycolysis. Model simulations reveal a single steady state whose position on the glycolysis-OXPHOS phase plane depends on environmental conditions, namely, oxygen concentration, infection, and extracellular lactate. We identify four metabolic regimes, determined by sufficiency of energy production and the driving process (OXPHOS or glycolysis). Decreasing the oxygen shifts cells from OXPHOS to glycolysis dominance in both infected and non-infected states, but infected cells may become energy-deficient even with sufficient oxygen due to virus-induced mitochondrial damage. Rising extracellular lactate initially promotes glycolysis but ultimately suppresses it at high levels, pushing cells into severe energy deficit with inhibited glycolysis. Simulations of reoxygenation exhibit hysteresis: cells pass through an energy-deficient zone during hypoxia onset but return through a safer trajectory when oxygen is restored; a vulnerability is higher in infected cells. Overall, the model clarifies metabolic trajectories during viral infection, suggesting that early hypoxia is particularly dangerous and that severe acidosis can further collapse energy production. Preventing or rapidly reversing hypoxia in respiratory infection may protect cells from energy failure and limit harmful lactate accumulation.
abstract_zh: 细胞通常将糖酵解与氧化磷酸化（OXPHOS）结合以满足能量需求，但在病理条件下这种平衡会发生改变。在SARS-CoV-2感染期间，缺氧、病毒入侵及组织乳酸升高会改变细胞代谢。为探究这些效应，我们提出一个简约数学模型，描述氧水平、病毒浸润和细胞外乳酸如何通过细胞内的HIF-1α蛋白共同调节代谢平衡，并考虑乳酸对糖酵解的双相、非单调影响。模型模拟揭示存在单一稳态，其在糖酵解-OXPHOS相平面上的位置取决于环境条件，即氧浓度、感染状态和细胞外乳酸。我们识别出四种代谢模式，由能量产生的充分性和驱动过程（OXPHOS或糖酵解）决定。降低氧水平使细胞在感染和非感染状态下均从OXPHOS主导转向糖酵解主导，但感染细胞即使在氧充足时也可能因病毒诱导的线粒体损伤而出现能量不足。细胞外乳酸升高最初促进糖酵解，但在高水平时最终抑制之，将细胞推入糖酵解受抑的严重能量缺乏状态。复氧模拟表现出滞后现象：细胞在缺氧发生期间穿过能量缺乏区，但在氧恢复时通过更安全轨迹返回；感染细胞的脆弱性更高。总体而言，该模型阐明了病毒感染期间的代谢轨迹，提示早期缺氧尤为危险，而严重酸中毒可进一步破坏能量产生。在呼吸道感染中预防或快速逆转缺氧可能保护细胞免于能量衰竭，并限制有害乳酸积累。
